issue: Under 18 U.S.C. § 3553(f)(1), does the introductory phrase "does not have" distribute across the three conjunctive criminal-history conditions, so that a defendant who has any one of them (such as a prior 3-point offense) is ineligible for safety valve relief?

sides.position: The phrase "does not have" distributes across each condition in § 3553(f)(1)(A)-(C), so a defendant is ineligible for safety valve relief if she has any one of the three disqualifying characteristics.
cases: United States v. Palomares, 52 F.4th 640 (5th Cir. 2022)
United States v. Pulsifer, 39 F.4th 1018 (8th Cir. 2022)

sides.position: The distributive reading is rejected. Section 3553(f)(1) is read disjunctively, or otherwise not as distributing "does not have" across each condition, so a defendant who has only one disqualifying characteristic may still be eligible.
cases: United States v. Lopez, 998 F.3d 431 (9th Cir. 2021)
United States v. Pace, 48 F.4th 741 (7th Cir. 2022)

this_court: The Fifth Circuit adopts the distributive reading. A defendant with a prior 3-point offense is ineligible for safety valve relief, so the court affirms.
quote: A circuit split has emerged over this issue.
cite: United States v. Palomares, 52 F.4th 640 (5th Cir. 2022)
